Step 6: Continuous integration

CI installs the PDF system libraries, runs the tests, and does a smoke render. .github/workflows/ci.yml:

name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: System libraries for WeasyPrint
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - run: uv sync
      - run: uvx ruff check src tests
      - run: uv run pytest -q
      - name: Smoke render
        run: |
          printf -- '---\ntitle: CI\n---\n\n## ok\n' | uv run rupa -o out/ci.pdf
          uv run rupa verify out/ci.pdf

Checkpoint: push to GitHub and confirm the workflow is green.

Step 7: The Claude Code plugin

Create the three plugin files.

plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:

{
  "name": "rupa",
  "displayName": "Rupa",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Write Markdown, let Rupa render the HTML or PDF. Keeps markup out of Claude's output tokens.",
  "author": { "name": "Vajra Sarpa", "url": "https://vajrasarpa.com" },
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["render", "pdf", "html", "markdown"]
}

plugin/skills/render/SKILL.md. The description line is the only part loaded every session, so it carries the whole instruction in one sentence:

---
name: render
description: Use when the user wants an HTML page or PDF document. Write Markdown, render it with the rupa CLI, then verify the PDF. Never hand-write HTML, CSS, or PDF code.
---

# Rendering with Rupa

## Render

1. Write the content as Markdown. Optional frontmatter keys: `title`,
   `subtitle`, `author`, `date`, `theme`, `toc` (true/false), `pages`.
   No other keys. If the user asks for a page count, set `pages: N`: Rupa
   then fits the PDF to N pages itself (drops the contents list, tightens
   type). Plan about 30 lines per page: a line of prose is about 15 words,
   and each code line, table row, list item and heading is one line.
2. Use `#` for parts, `##` for sections, `###` for subsections.
   Fenced code blocks take a language tag. Images are relative paths to
   files next to the Markdown file (or `data:image` URIs), never URLs.
3. Render with one command, using the extension the user asked for:

   ```bash
   rupa draft.md -o out/report.pdf
   ```

4. Read only the one-line status. Do not open or print the output file.
5. On a non-zero exit, fix the Markdown: `3` bad input and `4` render
   failure explain themselves on stderr; `5` means the PDF is still over
   `pages` and the status line says about how many lines to cut. Cut that
   many by rewriting the whole Markdown file with one Write, not a series
   of Edits, then render again. Do not measure pages yourself.

## Verify (PDF)

1. Run `rupa verify out/report.pdf` (add `--wants wants.yaml` if the project
   has one). It prints one line and writes `verify.json` plus sheet images.
2. If the status line reports no sheets, the PDF passed: skip to step 6.
   Do not render or open page images yourself.
   Otherwise read `verify.json`, then open each sheet image listed under `sheets`.
   Each sheet shows the theme's reference page on the left and the rendered
   page on the right.
3. Judge every sheet against each item in `rubric`. Record one line per
   sheet: `p<N> <kind>: PASS` or `p<N> <kind>: FAIL <rubric item> - <what>`.
4. Fix failures in the Markdown only: split a wide table, shorten a long
   code line, move or trim content around an awkward break. Make each
   round's fixes with one Write of the whole file, then render and verify
   again. Stop after two fix rounds.
5. If a failure can only be fixed in the theme (CSS), do not edit CSS.
   Report it to the user as a theme issue.
6. Tell the user the final check line and your per-sheet verdicts in a few
   lines.

Do not add styling to the Markdown. A different look is a theme change.

plugin/hooks/hooks.json. It prints a warning at session start only if the CLI is missing:

{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "command -v rupa >/dev/null || echo 'rupa CLI not on PATH: run uv tool install <path-to-rupa>'"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Validate and load it:

claude plugin validate ./plugin
# √ Validation passed

claude --plugin-dir ./plugin

Plugin names can't start with claude- or anthropic-; rupa is fine.

Checkpoint: inside that session, ask Claude whether a skill named rupa:render is available. It should say yes. Then ask for a one-page PDF on any topic and check that it wrote Markdown and called rupa, rather than writing HTML.

Step 8: Verification

src/rupa/verify.py holds both tiers. It builds a small page model from the PDF (lines with size, weight and position; fill; table area; share of monospace text), runs the checks on that model, and writes the sheets. Keeping the checks on a plain model rather than on pdfplumber objects is what makes them unit-testable.

Two traps found while building it:

  • WeasyPrint paints the page background as one large white rectangle. Left in, it makes every page look 100% full and turns every page into a "table". The code filters it out before measuring.
  • The cover page ends in a forced page break after the contents, so it is often short by design. It is exempt from the fill checks, as is the last page.
  • A reference page that spills onto a second page is a broken reference: the review compares against half a page. The visual review of this document caught exactly that after a sample edit, so rupa refs now refuses a sample whose page for any type runs over.
"""Verify a rendered PDF against a wants file.

Two tiers:
  1. Deterministic checks, run here in code: color, size, page count, empty
     pages, stranded headings, overflow. Free and repeatable.
  2. Evidence for a vision review: a side-by-side sheet (reference page |
     rendered page) for every flagged page, and with sample: per-type one
     per page type too. Rupa never calls
     a model; Claude reads the sheets and judges them against the rubric.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from importlib import resources
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

PT_PER_IN = 72
PAGE_SIZES = {"letter": (612, 792), "a4": (595, 842)}
# Body box from print.css (@page margins). Footer sits below BODY_BOTTOM.
MARGIN_TOP, MARGIN_SIDE, MARGIN_BOTTOM = 0.85, 0.8, 0.9
FOOTER_CUTOFF = 0.8  # inches from the bottom edge; lines below are footer
PART_HEADING_PT = 18  # an H1 "part" title is at least this size
HEADING_PT = 11.5  # bold, non-mono text at least this size is a heading

ALL_CHECKS = (
    "text-color",
    "page-size",
    "max-pages",
    "blank-page",
    "near-empty",
    "sparse",
    "heading-at-bottom",
    "overflow",
)
DEFAULT_RUBRIC = [
    "hierarchy: titles, headings and body read in the same order and weight as the reference",
    "spacing: margins, gaps and alignment match the reference; nothing crowded or floating",
    "overflow: no text, table or code is clipped, cut off or running into the margin",
    "page balance: no awkward breaks (a lone row, a stranded heading, a near-empty page)",
    "style: colors, rules and boxes match the reference; text is solid black",
]
SAMPLE_MODES = ("per-type", "flagged", "all", "none")
DEFAULT_WANTS = {
    "theme": "default",
    "page_size": "letter",
    "max_pages": 100,
    "text_color": "#000000",
    "sparse_fill": 0.4,
    "near_empty_fill": 0.2,
    "checks": list(ALL_CHECKS),
    "vision": {
        "sample": "flagged",
        "max_sheets": 8,
        "resolution": 90,
        "rubric": DEFAULT_RUBRIC,
    },
}
EXIT_CHECKS_FAILED = 5


class WantsError(ValueError):
    """Raised for an unreadable or invalid wants file."""


class PdfError(ValueError):
    """Raised when the file given to verify cannot be read as a PDF."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- wants


def load_wants(path: str | None) -> dict:
    wants = json.loads(json.dumps(DEFAULT_WANTS))  # deep copy
    if not path:
        return wants
    try:
        given = yaml.safe_load(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as exc:
        raise WantsError(f"cannot read wants file: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(given, dict):
        raise WantsError("wants file must be a YAML mapping")
    unknown = set(given) - set(DEFAULT_WANTS)
    if unknown:
        raise WantsError(f"unknown wants keys: {sorted(unknown)}")
    vision = given.pop("vision", {}) or {}
    if not isinstance(vision, dict):
        raise WantsError("vision must be a YAML mapping")
    unknown_v = set(vision) - set(DEFAULT_WANTS["vision"])
    if unknown_v:
        raise WantsError(f"unknown vision keys: {sorted(unknown_v)}")
    wants.update(given)
    wants["vision"].update(vision)
    _validate(wants)
    return wants


def _is_int(value) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def _is_fraction(value) -> bool:
    return (
        isinstance(value, (int, float))
        and not isinstance(value, bool)
        and (0 <= value <= 1)
    )


def _is_str_list(value) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(v, str) for v in value)


def _validate(wants: dict) -> None:
    """Reject bad values here, so verify() never fails halfway with a traceback."""
    from .render import THEMES

    vision = wants["vision"]
    if wants["theme"] not in THEMES:
        raise WantsError(f"theme must be one of {list(THEMES)}")
    if wants["page_size"] not in PAGE_SIZES:
        raise WantsError(f"page_size must be one of {sorted(PAGE_SIZES)}")
    if not _is_int(wants["max_pages"]) or wants["max_pages"] < 1:
        raise WantsError("max_pages must be a whole number of at least 1")
    color = wants["text_color"]
    if not (isinstance(color, str) and re.fullmatch(r"#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}", color)):
        raise WantsError(f"text_color must be #RRGGBB, got {color!r}")
    for key in ("sparse_fill", "near_empty_fill"):
        if not _is_fraction(wants[key]):
            raise WantsError(f"{key} must be a number from 0 to 1")
    if not _is_str_list(wants["checks"]):
        raise WantsError("checks must be a list of check names")
    bad = set(wants["checks"]) - set(ALL_CHECKS)
    if bad:
        raise WantsError(f"unknown checks: {sorted(bad)}")
    if vision["sample"] not in SAMPLE_MODES:
        raise WantsError(f"vision.sample must be one of {', '.join(SAMPLE_MODES)}")
    if not _is_int(vision["max_sheets"]) or vision["max_sheets"] < 0:
        raise WantsError("vision.max_sheets must be a whole number of at least 0")
    if not _is_int(vision["resolution"]) or not 30 <= vision["resolution"] <= 300:
        raise WantsError("vision.resolution must be a whole number from 30 to 300")
    if not _is_str_list(vision["rubric"]):
        raise WantsError("vision.rubric must be a list of strings")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- page model


@dataclass
class Line:
    top: float
    bottom: float
    x0: float
    x1: float
    size: float
    mono: bool
    bold: bool
    text: str


@dataclass
class PageInfo:
    number: int
    width: float
    height: float
    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)  # body lines only, no footer
    colors: list[tuple] = field(
        default_factory=list
    )  # one entry per distinct color seen
    off_colors: int = 0  # number of chars not matching the wanted color
    content_bottom: float = 0.0
    table_frac: float = 0.0
    kind: str = "prose"

    @property
    def body_top(self) -> float:
        return MARGIN_TOP * PT_PER_IN

    @property
    def body_bottom(self) -> float:
        return self.height - MARGIN_BOTTOM * PT_PER_IN

    @property
    def fill(self) -> float:
        if not self.lines:
            return 0.0
        span = self.body_bottom - self.body_top
        return max(0.0, min(1.0, (self.content_bottom - self.body_top) / span))

    @property
    def mono_frac(self) -> float:
        chars = sum(len(ln.text) for ln in self.lines) or 1
        return sum(len(ln.text) for ln in self.lines if ln.mono) / chars

    @property
    def starts_part(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.lines) and self.lines[0].size >= PART_HEADING_PT


def _hex_to_rgb(value: str) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    v = value.lstrip("#")
    if len(v) != 6:
        raise WantsError(f"text_color must be #RRGGBB, got {value!r}")
    return tuple(int(v[i : i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (0, 2, 4))


def _to_rgb(color) -> tuple[float, float, float] | None:
    """Normalize a pdfplumber color (gray, RGB or CMYK tuple) to RGB."""
    if color is None:
        return None
    c = tuple(color) if isinstance(color, (list, tuple)) else (color,)
    if len(c) == 1:
        return (c[0], c[0], c[0])
    if len(c) == 3:
        return c
    if len(c) == 4:
        cy, m, y, k = c
        return ((1 - cy) * (1 - k), (1 - m) * (1 - k), (1 - y) * (1 - k))
    return None


def _same_color(a, b, tol: float = 0.01) -> bool:
    return a is not None and all(abs(x - y) <= tol for x, y in zip(a, b))


def read_pages(pdf_path: str | Path, wanted_color: str = "#000000") -> list[PageInfo]:
    import pdfplumber

    want = _hex_to_rgb(wanted_color)
    try:
        return _read_pages(pdfplumber, pdf_path, want)
    except Exception as exc:  # pdfminer raises many types on a damaged file
        raise PdfError(f"cannot read PDF {pdf_path}: {exc}") from exc


def _read_pages(pdfplumber, pdf_path, want) -> list[PageInfo]:
    pages: list[PageInfo] = []
    with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
        for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
            info = PageInfo(
                number=i, width=float(page.width), height=float(page.height)
            )
            seen: set = set()
            for ch in page.chars:
                rgb = _to_rgb(ch.get("non_stroking_color"))
                seen.add(rgb)
                if not _same_color(rgb, want):
                    info.off_colors += 1
            info.colors = sorted(c for c in seen if c is not None)
            footer_y = info.height - FOOTER_CUTOFF * PT_PER_IN
            for tl in page.extract_text_lines(return_chars=True):
                if tl["top"] >= footer_y or not tl["chars"]:
                    continue
                chars = tl["chars"]
                fonts = [c.get("fontname", "") for c in chars]
                info.lines.append(
                    Line(
                        top=tl["top"],
                        bottom=tl["bottom"],
                        x0=tl["x0"],
                        x1=tl["x1"],
                        size=max(c["size"] for c in chars),
                        mono=sum("Mono" in f for f in fonts) > len(fonts) / 2,
                        bold=sum(
                            any(w in f for w in ("Bold", "SemiBold", "Black"))
                            for f in fonts
                        )
                        > len(fonts) / 2,
                        text=tl["text"],
                    )
                )
            body_h = info.body_bottom - info.body_top
            # The page background is painted as one big white rect; ignore it and
            # anything else that spans nearly the whole body.
            rects = [
                r
                for r in page.rects
                if r["bottom"] < footer_y and r["height"] < 0.95 * body_h
            ]
            line_bottoms = [ln.bottom for ln in info.lines]
            info.content_bottom = max(
                [r["bottom"] for r in rects] + line_bottoms, default=0.0
            )
            body_area = (info.width - 2 * MARGIN_SIDE * PT_PER_IN) * body_h
            big = 0.95 * body_h
            no_bg = page.filter(
                lambda o, big=big: (
                    not (o.get("object_type") == "rect" and o["height"] >= big)
                )
            )
            tables = [t for t in no_bg.find_tables() if len(t.columns) >= 2]
            table_area = sum(
                (t.bbox[2] - t.bbox[0]) * (t.bbox[3] - t.bbox[1]) for t in tables
            )
            info.table_frac = min(1.0, table_area / body_area) if body_area else 0.0
            info.kind = classify(info)
            pages.append(info)
    return pages


def classify(p: PageInfo) -> str:
    if p.number == 1:
        return "cover"
    if p.mono_frac > 0.5:
        return "code"
    if p.table_frac > 0.3:
        return "table"
    return "prose"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- checks


@dataclass
class CheckResult:
    id: str
    ok: bool
    pages: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    detail: str = ""


def run_checks(pages: list[PageInfo], wants: dict) -> list[CheckResult]:
    enabled = wants["checks"]
    results: list[CheckResult] = []
    last = len(pages)

    def add(cid: str, bad: list[int], detail: str) -> None:
        if cid in enabled:
            results.append(CheckResult(cid, not bad, bad, detail if bad else ""))

    add(
        "text-color",
        [p.number for p in pages if p.off_colors],
        f"text not {wants['text_color']}",
    )
    w, h = PAGE_SIZES[wants["page_size"]]
    add(
        "page-size",
        [p.number for p in pages if abs(p.width - w) > 1 or abs(p.height - h) > 1],
        f"page is not {wants['page_size']}",
    )
    add(
        "max-pages",
        list(range(wants["max_pages"] + 1, last + 1)),
        f"{last} pages > max {wants['max_pages']}",
    )
    add("blank-page", [p.number for p in pages if not p.lines], "page has no text")

    near_empty = [
        p.number
        for p in pages
        # The cover (page 1) ends in a forced break and the last page ends the
        # document, so neither is judged on how full it is.
        if p.lines and p.number not in (1, last) and p.fill < wants["near_empty_fill"]
    ]
    add("near-empty", near_empty, f"under {wants['near_empty_fill']:.0%} full")

    sparse = []
    for idx, p in enumerate(pages):
        if not p.lines or p.number in (1, last) or p.number in near_empty:
            continue
        next_starts_part = idx + 1 < last and pages[idx + 1].starts_part
        if p.fill < wants["sparse_fill"] and not next_starts_part:
            sparse.append(p.number)
    add(
        "sparse",
        sparse,
        f"under {wants['sparse_fill']:.0%} full with no part break after",
    )

    def is_heading(ln: Line) -> bool:
        return ln.bold and not ln.mono and ln.size >= HEADING_PT

    stranded = []
    # The last page is exempt: nothing follows its final line, so no page break
    # separated a heading from its content (this also covers a title-only doc).
    for idx, p in enumerate(pages[:-1]):
        if not p.lines:
            continue
        if is_heading(p.lines[-1]):
            stranded.append(p.number)
            continue
        # A heading and a one-line lead-in ("Run this:") whose block moved to
        # the next page. A complete one-line section before a new heading is fine.
        nxt = pages[idx + 1].lines
        if (
            len(p.lines) >= 2
            and is_heading(head := p.lines[-2])
            and p.lines[-1].top - head.bottom < 2 * head.size  # directly under it
            and nxt
            and not is_heading(nxt[0])
        ):
            stranded.append(p.number)
    add(
        "heading-at-bottom",
        stranded,
        "heading is the last line, or a heading and one line end the page",
    )

    overflow = []
    for p in pages:
        left = MARGIN_SIDE * PT_PER_IN - 2
        right = p.width - MARGIN_SIDE * PT_PER_IN + 2
        if any(ln.x0 < left or ln.x1 > right for ln in p.lines):
            overflow.append(p.number)
    add("overflow", overflow, "text extends past the side margins")
    return results


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sampling + sheets


def sample_pages(
    pages: list[PageInfo], results: list[CheckResult], wants: dict
) -> list[PageInfo]:
    """Flagged pages first, then one representative (the middle one) per page kind.

    "flagged" stops after the flagged pages, so a clean PDF gets no sheets.
    """
    mode = wants["vision"]["sample"]
    if mode == "none":
        return []
    if mode == "all":
        return pages[: wants["vision"]["max_sheets"]]
    flagged = sorted({n for r in results for n in r.pages if n <= len(pages)})
    chosen: list[int] = list(flagged)
    for kind in () if mode == "flagged" else ("cover", "prose", "table", "code"):
        of_kind = [p.number for p in pages if p.kind == kind]
        if of_kind and not any(n in of_kind for n in chosen):
            chosen.append(of_kind[len(of_kind) // 2])
    by_number = {p.number: p for p in pages}
    return [by_number[n] for n in chosen[: wants["vision"]["max_sheets"]]]


def reference_path(theme: str, kind: str):
    ref = resources.files("rupa") / "references" / theme / f"{kind}.png"
    return ref if ref.is_file() else None


def _label(img, text: str):
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

    strip = 28
    out = Image.new("RGB", (img.width, img.height + strip), "white")
    out.paste(img, (0, strip))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(out)
    try:
        font = ImageFont.load_default(size=16)
    except TypeError:  # Pillow < 10.1
        font = ImageFont.load_default()
    draw.text((8, 5), text, fill="black", font=font)
    return out


def render_page_png(pdf_path: str | Path, number: int, resolution: int):
    import pdfplumber

    with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
        return (
            pdf.pages[number - 1]
            .to_image(resolution=resolution)
            .original.convert("RGB")
        )


def make_sheet(
    pdf_path, page: PageInfo, flags: list[str], theme: str, resolution: int, out: Path
) -> Path:
    from PIL import Image

    rendered = render_page_png(pdf_path, page.number, resolution)
    right = _label(
        rendered,
        f"PAGE {page.number} ({page.kind})"
        + (f"  FLAGGED: {', '.join(flags)}" if flags else ""),
    )
    ref = reference_path(theme, page.kind)
    if ref is None:
        sheet = right
    else:
        with resources.as_file(ref) as ref_file:
            ref_img = Image.open(ref_file).convert("RGB")
            ref_img = ref_img.resize(
                (
                    round(ref_img.width * rendered.height / ref_img.height),
                    rendered.height,
                )
            )
        left = _label(ref_img, f"REFERENCE: {page.kind} ({theme})")
        sheet = Image.new(
            "RGB", (left.width + right.width + 16, right.height), (148, 163, 184)
        )
        sheet.paste(left, (0, 0))
        sheet.paste(right, (left.width + 16, 0))
    path = out / f"sheet-p{page.number:03d}-{page.kind}.png"
    sheet.save(path, optimize=True)
    return path


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- entry point


@dataclass
class VerifyReport:
    pdf: str
    pages: int
    checks: list[CheckResult]
    sheets: list[dict]
    rubric: list[str]
    manifest: str = ""

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return all(c.ok for c in self.checks)

    def summary(self) -> str:
        passed = sum(c.ok for c in self.checks)
        fails = [
            f"{c.id} p{','.join(map(str, c.pages[:6]))}"
            for c in self.checks
            if not c.ok
        ]
        line = f"verify: {passed}/{len(self.checks)} checks pass"
        if fails:
            line += f" (FAIL {'; '.join(fails)})"
        if self.sheets:
            n = len(self.sheets)
            line += (
                f"; {n} sheet{'s' if n != 1 else ''} for visual review"
                f" in {Path(self.manifest).parent}/"
            )
        return line


def verify(
    pdf_path: str | Path, wants: dict, out_dir: str | Path, theme: str | None = None
) -> VerifyReport:
    theme = theme or wants["theme"]
    out = Path(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for old in out.glob("sheet-p*.png"):
        old.unlink()
    pages = read_pages(pdf_path, wants["text_color"])
    results = run_checks(pages, wants)
    flags_by_page: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
    for r in results:
        for n in r.pages:
            flags_by_page.setdefault(n, []).append(r.id)
    sheets = []
    for p in sample_pages(pages, results, wants):
        flags = flags_by_page.get(p.number, [])
        path = make_sheet(pdf_path, p, flags, theme, wants["vision"]["resolution"], out)
        sheets.append(
            {"path": str(path), "page": p.number, "kind": p.kind, "flags": flags}
        )
    report = VerifyReport(
        pdf=str(pdf_path),
        pages=len(pages),
        checks=results,
        sheets=sheets,
        rubric=wants["vision"]["rubric"],
        manifest=str(out / "verify.json"),
    )
    Path(report.manifest).write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "pdf": report.pdf,
                "pages": report.pages,
                "ok": report.ok,
                "checks": [asdict(c) for c in results],
                "sheets": sheets,
                "rubric": report.rubric,
            },
            indent=2,
        )
    )
    return report


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- references


def build_references(
    pdf_path: str | Path, out_dir: str | Path, resolution: int = 90
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Save the most typical page of each kind in a sample render as <kind>.png.

    Raises ValueError if the sample is missing a page kind, or if a picked page
    spills onto the next page, since a reference must show one whole page.
    """
    pages = read_pages(pdf_path)
    best: dict[str, PageInfo] = {}
    score = {
        "cover": lambda p: 1,
        "code": lambda p: p.mono_frac * p.fill,
        "table": lambda p: p.table_frac * p.fill,
        "prose": lambda p: p.fill,
    }
    for p in pages:
        if p.kind not in best or score[p.kind](p) > score[p.kind](best[p.kind]):
            best[p.kind] = p
    missing = {"cover", "prose", "table", "code"} - set(best)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"sample has no {sorted(missing)} page; extend it")
    for kind, p in best.items():
        nxt = p.number  # pages are 1-based, so this indexes the following page
        if kind != "cover" and nxt < len(pages) and pages[nxt].kind == kind:
            raise ValueError(f"sample {kind} page p{p.number} spills over; trim it")
    out = Path(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for kind, p in best.items():
        render_page_png(pdf_path, p.number, resolution).save(
            out / f"{kind}.png", optimize=True
        )
    return {kind: p.number for kind, p in best.items()}

The sample document every theme's reference pages come from, src/rupa/references/sample.md. Each section is sized to fill one page of its type:

---
title: Reference Sample
subtitle: The page types every Rupa theme is compared against
author: Rupa
date: Reference
---

## Introduction

Rupa separates content from form. Claude writes Markdown, and the renderer applies every visual decision in one place, the same way each time. This paragraph exists to show how body text, spacing and rhythm look on a full page of prose, so a reviewer can compare a rendered page against it.

The wants file with every default spelled out, wants.example.yaml. A test keeps it in sync with the code:

# What a finished PDF must satisfy. Every key is optional; omitted keys use
# the defaults shown here. Unknown keys are an error.
theme: default            # whose reference pages the sheets compare against
page_size: letter         # letter | a4
max_pages: 100
text_color: "#000000"     # every character must be this color
sparse_fill: 0.4          # flag a page under 40% full, unless a part starts next
near_empty_fill: 0.2      # flag a page under 20% full, always
checks:                   # remove any you don't want
  - text-color
  - page-size
  - max-pages
  - blank-page
  - near-empty
  - sparse
  - heading-at-bottom
  - overflow
vision:
  sample: flagged         # flagged | per-type | all | none (per-type: flagged pages plus one of each kind)
  max_sheets: 8           # cap on sheet images per run
  resolution: 90          # DPI for page images; ~1,500 x 1,000 px per sheet
  rubric:                 # what Claude judges on each sheet
    - "hierarchy: titles, headings and body read in the same order and weight as the reference"
    - "spacing: margins, gaps and alignment match the reference; nothing crowded or floating"
    - "overflow: no text, table or code is clipped, cut off or running into the margin"
    - "page balance: no awkward breaks (a lone row, a stranded heading, a near-empty page)"
    - "style: colors, rules and boxes match the reference; text is solid black"

The tests, tests/test_verify.py. Most build synthetic pages, so each check is tested in isolation, and two run against a real render:

import json

import pytest

from rupa.cli import EXIT_CHECKS, EXIT_INPUT, EXIT_OK, main
from rupa.document import parse
from rupa.render import to_pdf
from rupa.verify import (
    DEFAULT_WANTS,
    Line,
    PageInfo,
    WantsError,
    _to_rgb,
    load_wants,
    run_checks,
    sample_pages,
    verify,
)

LETTER = (612.0, 792.0)


def body_line(top, size=10.5, bold=False, mono=False, x0=60.0, x1=500.0):
    return Line(top, top + size, x0, x1, size, mono, bold, "text")


def page(n, fill_to=700.0, lines=None, **kw):
    lines = lines if lines is not None else [body_line(70), body_line(fill_to - 10.5)]
    p = PageInfo(number=n, width=LETTER[0], height=LETTER[1], lines=lines, **kw)
    p.content_bottom = max((ln.bottom for ln in lines), default=0.0)
    return p


def failing(results):
    return {r.id: r.pages for r in results if not r.ok}


# ---- wants file


def test_defaults_without_a_file():
    assert load_wants(None) == DEFAULT_WANTS


def test_wants_file_overrides_and_merges_vision(tmp_path):
    f = tmp_path / "wants.yaml"
    f.write_text("max_pages: 3\nvision:\n  max_sheets: 2\n")
    wants = load_wants(str(f))
    assert wants["max_pages"] == 3
    assert wants["vision"]["max_sheets"] == 2
    assert wants["vision"]["sample"] == "flagged"  # untouched default survives


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "body, message",
    [
        ("colour: red\n", "unknown wants keys"),
        ("checks: [nope]\n", "unknown checks"),
        ("page_size: a5\n", "page_size"),
        ("vision:\n  model: big\n", "unknown vision keys"),
        ('text_color: "#GGG"\n', "text_color"),
        ('text_color: "#GGGGGG"\n', "text_color"),
        ('max_pages: "10"\n', "max_pages"),
        ("checks: null\n", "checks must be a list"),
        ("sparse_fill: 2\n", "sparse_fill"),
        ("theme: ../../etc\n", "theme must be one of"),
        ("vision: 5\n", "vision must be a YAML mapping"),
        ("vision:\n  resolution: 5000\n", "vision.resolution"),
    ],
)
def test_bad_wants_are_rejected(tmp_path, body, message):
    f = tmp_path / "wants.yaml"
    f.write_text(body)
    with pytest.raises(WantsError, match=message):
        load_wants(str(f))


# ---- colors


def test_color_normalization_handles_gray_rgb_and_cmyk():
    assert _to_rgb((0,)) == (0, 0, 0)
    assert _to_rgb((0.0, 0.0, 0.0)) == (0, 0, 0)
    assert _to_rgb((0, 0, 0, 1)) == (0, 0, 0)
    assert _to_rgb(None) is None


# ---- deterministic checks on synthetic pages


def test_clean_document_passes_everything():
    pages = [page(1), page(2), page(3)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {}


def test_off_color_text_fails():
    pages = [page(1), page(2, off_colors=12)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {"text-color": [2]}


def test_wrong_page_size_fails():
    pages = [page(1)]
    pages[0].width, pages[0].height = 595.0, 842.0  # A4
    assert "page-size" in failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None)))


def test_near_empty_page_fails_but_last_page_is_exempt():
    pages = [page(1), page(2, fill_to=120), page(3), page(4, fill_to=120)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {"near-empty": [2]}


def test_sparse_page_is_allowed_before_a_part_break():
    part = [body_line(70, size=20, bold=True), body_line(700)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, fill_to=300), page(3, lines=part), page(4)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {}


def test_sparse_page_without_a_part_break_fails():
    pages = [page(1), page(2, fill_to=300), page(3), page(4)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {"sparse": [2]}


def test_stranded_heading_fails():
    lines = [body_line(70), body_line(690, size=15, bold=True)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, lines=lines), page(3)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {"heading-at-bottom": [2]}


def test_heading_and_lead_in_before_moved_block_fails():
    lines = [body_line(70), body_line(670, size=15, bold=True), body_line(690)]
    nxt = [body_line(70, mono=True), body_line(700)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, lines=lines), page(3, lines=nxt)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {"heading-at-bottom": [2]}


def test_one_line_section_before_next_heading_passes():
    lines = [body_line(70), body_line(670, size=15, bold=True), body_line(690)]
    nxt = [body_line(70, size=15, bold=True), body_line(700)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, lines=lines), page(3, lines=nxt)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {}


def test_title_only_document_is_not_a_stranded_heading():
    pages = [page(1, lines=[body_line(70, size=26, bold=True)])]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {}


def test_heading_ending_the_last_page_is_not_stranded():
    lines = [body_line(70), body_line(690, size=15, bold=True)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2), page(3, lines=lines)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {}


def test_heading_only_section_after_toc_passes_verify(tmp_path):
    data, _ = to_pdf(parse("---\ntitle: CI\n---\n\n## ok\n"))
    pdf = tmp_path / "ci.pdf"
    pdf.write_bytes(data)
    assert verify(pdf, load_wants(None), tmp_path / "v").ok


def test_title_only_render_passes_verify(tmp_path):
    data, _ = to_pdf(parse("# Hello\n"))
    pdf = tmp_path / "hello.pdf"
    pdf.write_bytes(data)
    report = verify(pdf, load_wants(None), tmp_path / "v")
    assert report.summary() == "verify: 8/8 checks pass"  # clean: no sheets
    wants = load_wants(None)
    wants["vision"]["sample"] = "per-type"
    report = verify(pdf, wants, tmp_path / "v")
    assert report.ok, report.summary()
    assert "1 sheet for visual review" in report.summary()


def test_bold_code_at_bottom_is_not_a_heading():
    lines = [body_line(70), body_line(690, size=12, bold=True, mono=True)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, lines=lines), page(3)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {}


def test_text_past_the_margin_fails():
    lines = [body_line(70), body_line(690, x1=600)]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, lines=lines), page(3)]
    assert failing(run_checks(pages, load_wants(None))) == {"overflow": [2]}


def test_disabled_checks_are_skipped():
    wants = load_wants(None)
    wants["checks"] = ["text-color"]
    pages = [page(1), page(2, fill_to=120), page(3)]
    results = run_checks(pages, wants)
    assert [r.id for r in results] == ["text-color"]


# ---- sampling


def test_sampling_takes_flagged_pages_then_one_per_kind():
    pages = [page(1, kind="cover")] + [page(n, kind="prose") for n in range(2, 9)]
    pages.append(page(9, kind="code"))
    wants = load_wants(None)
    wants["vision"]["sample"] = "per-type"
    pages[3].off_colors = 1  # page 4 flagged
    picked = [p.number for p in sample_pages(pages, run_checks(pages, wants), wants)]
    assert picked[0] == 4  # flagged first
    assert 1 in picked and 9 in picked  # cover and code represented
    assert sum(pages[n - 1].kind == "prose" for n in picked) == 1  # prose covered once


def test_sampling_flagged_takes_only_flagged_pages():
    pages = [page(1, kind="cover")] + [page(n, kind="prose") for n in range(2, 6)]
    wants = load_wants(None)  # default: flagged
    assert sample_pages(pages, run_checks(pages, wants), wants) == []
    pages[2].off_colors = 1  # page 3 flagged
    picked = [p.number for p in sample_pages(pages, run_checks(pages, wants), wants)]
    assert picked == [3]


def test_sampling_none_returns_nothing():
    wants = load_wants(None)
    wants["vision"]["sample"] = "none"
    assert sample_pages([page(1)], [], wants) == []


# ---- end to end on a real render

DOC = """---
title: Verify me
---

## Section

Some body text that renders black.

| a | b |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
"""


@pytest.fixture
def real_pdf(tmp_path):
    data, _ = to_pdf(parse(DOC))
    path = tmp_path / "doc.pdf"
    path.write_bytes(data)
    return path


def test_real_render_passes_and_writes_sheets(real_pdf, tmp_path):
    wants = load_wants(None)
    wants["vision"]["sample"] = "per-type"
    report = verify(real_pdf, wants, tmp_path / "v")
    assert report.ok, report.summary()
    assert report.sheets and all(
        (tmp_path / "v" / s["path"].split("/")[-1]).exists() for s in report.sheets
    )
    manifest = json.loads((tmp_path / "v" / "verify.json").read_text())
    assert manifest["ok"] is True and manifest["rubric"]


def test_cli_verify_exit_codes(real_pdf, tmp_path, capsys):
    assert main(["verify", str(real_pdf), "--out", str(tmp_path / "a")]) == EXIT_OK
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.startswith("verify: ")

    strict = tmp_path / "wants.yaml"
    strict.write_text("max_pages: 1\n")  # cover + TOC page break makes 2 pages
    code = main(
        ["verify", str(real_pdf), "--wants", str(strict), "--out", str(tmp_path / "b")]
    )
    assert code == EXIT_CHECKS
    assert "FAIL max-pages" in capsys.readouterr().out

    bad = tmp_path / "bad.yaml"
    bad.write_text("nope: 1\n")
    code = main(["verify", str(real_pdf), "--wants", str(bad)])
    assert code == EXIT_INPUT


def test_example_wants_file_matches_defaults():
    from pathlib import Path

    example = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "wants.example.yaml"
    assert load_wants(str(example)) == DEFAULT_WANTS


def test_reference_sample_gives_one_whole_page_per_kind(tmp_path):
    from importlib import resources

    from rupa.verify import build_references

    sample = (resources.files("rupa") / "references" / "sample.md").read_text()
    data, _ = to_pdf(parse(sample))
    pdf = tmp_path / "sample.pdf"
    pdf.write_bytes(data)
    picked = build_references(pdf, tmp_path / "refs")
    assert set(picked) == {"cover", "prose", "table", "code"}
    assert all((tmp_path / "refs" / f"{k}.png").exists() for k in picked)


def test_references_refuse_a_spilling_sample(tmp_path):
    from rupa.verify import build_references

    code = "\n".join(f"x_{i} = {i}" for i in range(200))
    md = f"## Prose\n\nText.\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n\n```python\n{code}\n```\n"
    data, _ = to_pdf(parse(md))
    pdf = tmp_path / "s.pdf"
    pdf.write_bytes(data)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        build_references(pdf, tmp_path / "refs")

Step 9: Measure

bench/bench.sh sets up the four arms and runs them. The awk line builds the render-only plugin by dropping everything from ## Verify up to the skill's closing line, and the sed line builds the per-type plugin by adding --sample per-type to the verify command:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Compare Claude Code cost on the same task across four arms:
#   baseline       no plugin: Claude writes the HTML/CSS and finds its own PDF tool
#   rupa           plugin, render only (the skill's Verify section is removed)
#   rupa-pertype   plugin, verify with a sheet per page type as well as flagged pages
#   rupa-verify    plugin as shipped: render, then verify; sheets only for flagged pages
#
# Usage: bench/bench.sh [runs]        default 1 run per arm (a pilot)
#        MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 bench/bench.sh 3
#        TASK=guide bench/bench.sh 3    prompt from bench/tasks/<TASK>.txt
#                                        (default: report, a 2-page prose report)
#        ARMS="rupa rupa-verify" bench/bench.sh 3   only these arms (default: all four)
# Each run starts in a fresh empty directory, so no arm can see this repo.
set -euo pipefail

RUNS="${1:-1}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
TASK_NAME="${TASK:-report}"
TASK_FILE="$ROOT/bench/tasks/$TASK_NAME.txt"
[[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]] || { echo "bench: no task $TASK_FILE" >&2; exit 2; }
TASK_PROMPT="$(cat "$TASK_FILE")"
RESULTS="$ROOT/bench/results/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-$TASK_NAME"
TOOLS="Bash Write Read Edit Skill"
MODEL_FLAG=()
[[ -n "${MODEL:-}" ]] && MODEL_FLAG=(--model "$MODEL")

mkdir -p "$RESULTS"
cp "$TASK_FILE" "$RESULTS/task.txt"
command -v rupa >/dev/null || { echo "bench: rupa is not on PATH" >&2; exit 2; }

# Variant arms use a copy of the plugin with an edited skill.
# Copy only what loads, not evals/ and its results.
plugin_copy() {  # $1 = directory to create
  mkdir -p "$1"
  cp -r "$ROOT/plugin/.claude-plugin" "$ROOT/plugin/hooks" "$ROOT/plugin/skills" "$1/"
}
SKILL="$ROOT/plugin/skills/render/SKILL.md"

# Render only: the skill stops before "## Verify".
NOVERIFY="$RESULTS/plugin-noverify"
plugin_copy "$NOVERIFY"
awk '/^## Verify/ {skip=1} /^Do not add styling/ {skip=0} !skip' \
  "$SKILL" > "$NOVERIFY/skills/render/SKILL.md"

# Per-type: verify also makes one sheet per page type, even on a clean PDF.
PERTYPE="$RESULTS/plugin-pertype"
plugin_copy "$PERTYPE"
sed 's/`rupa verify out\/report.pdf`/`rupa verify --sample per-type out\/report.pdf`/' \
  "$SKILL" > "$PERTYPE/skills/render/SKILL.md"
grep -q -- '--sample per-type' "$PERTYPE/skills/render/SKILL.md" \
  || { echo "bench: could not make the per-type skill; SKILL.md changed?" >&2; exit 2; }

ARMS="${ARMS:-baseline rupa rupa-pertype rupa-verify}"

run_arm() {  # $1 = arm name, remaining args = extra claude flags
  local arm="$1"; shift
  [[ " $ARMS " == *" $arm "* ]] || return 0
  for i in $(seq 1 "$RUNS"); do
    local work; work="$(mktemp -d)"
    echo "bench: $arm run $i" >&2
    ( cd "$work" && claude -p "$TASK_PROMPT" --output-format json --allowedTools "$TOOLS" \
        ${MODEL_FLAG[@]+"${MODEL_FLAG[@]}"} "$@" ) > "$RESULTS/$arm-$i.json" 2> "$RESULTS/$arm-$i.err" || true
    if [[ -s "$work/report.pdf" ]]; then
      cp "$work/report.pdf" "$RESULTS/$arm-$i.pdf"
    fi
    rm -rf "$work"
  done
}

run_arm baseline
run_arm rupa --plugin-dir "$NOVERIFY"
run_arm rupa-pertype --plugin-dir "$PERTYPE"
run_arm rupa-verify --plugin-dir "$ROOT/plugin"

python3 "$ROOT/bench/summarize.py" "$RESULTS"

bench/summarize.py reads one results folder and prints the tables:

"""Summarize a bench results directory: one row per run, then medians per arm.

Turns and cache reads come first because they drive cost: every turn re-reads
the whole context from cache, while output tokens are a small share.
"""

import json
import statistics
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# rupa-flagged is the old name of the flagged arm, kept so older results read.
ARMS = ("baseline", "rupa", "rupa-flagged", "rupa-pertype", "rupa-verify")
COLS = ("turns", "cache_read", "cache_write", "input", "output", "cost_usd", "secs")


def row(path: Path) -> dict | None:
    try:
        r = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
    u = r.get("usage", {})
    return {
        "turns": r.get("num_turns", 0),
        "cache_read": u.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0),
        "cache_write": u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0),
        "input": u.get("input_tokens", 0),
        "output": u.get("output_tokens", 0),
        "cost_usd": r.get("total_cost_usd", 0.0),
        "secs": round(r.get("duration_ms", 0) / 1000),
        "pdf": path.with_suffix(".pdf").exists(),
    }


def fmt(v) -> str:
    if isinstance(v, float):
        return f"{v:.3f}"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "yes" if v else "NO"
    return f"{v:,}"


def main(results: Path) -> None:
    runs = {arm: [] for arm in ARMS}
    for f in sorted(results.glob("*.json")):
        arm = f.stem.rsplit("-", 1)[0]
        if arm in runs and (r := row(f)):
            runs[arm].append(r)
    arms = [a for a in ARMS if runs[a]]

    header = ("arm", "run", *COLS, "pdf")
    print("\t".join(header))
    for arm in arms:
        for i, r in enumerate(runs[arm], 1):
            print("\t".join([arm, str(i), *(fmt(r[c]) for c in COLS), fmt(r["pdf"])]))

    print("\nmedians (runs without a PDF excluded)")
    print("\t".join(("arm", "n", *COLS)))
    base = None
    for arm in arms:
        ok = [r for r in runs[arm] if r["pdf"]]
        if not ok:
            print(f"{arm}\t0\t(no successful runs)")
            continue
        med = {c: statistics.median(r[c] for r in ok) for c in COLS}
        med = {c: v if c == "cost_usd" else round(v) for c, v in med.items()}
        base = base or (med if arm == "baseline" else None)
        print("\t".join([arm, str(len(ok)), *(fmt(med[c]) for c in COLS)]))
    if base:
        print("\nvs baseline (median turns, median cost)")
        for arm in arms[1:]:
            ok = [r for r in runs[arm] if r["pdf"]]
            if ok and base["turns"] and base["cost_usd"]:
                t = statistics.median(r["turns"] for r in ok) / base["turns"] - 1
                c = statistics.median(r["cost_usd"] for r in ok) / base["cost_usd"] - 1
                print(f"{arm}\tturns {t:+.0%}\tcost {c:+.0%}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]))

Before spending anything, test the plumbing with a stand-in for claude that writes a fake report.pdf and prints canned JSON. During the build this showed each arm getting the right plugin and the summary computing the comparisons correctly. bench/fake/claude:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stand-in for `claude` to test bench.sh plumbing without spending tokens.
# Usage: PATH="$PWD/bench/fake:$PATH" bench/bench.sh 2
# Reports fewer turns for the plugin arms so the comparison lines have
# something to show. The numbers are made up; only the plumbing is real.
plugin=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do [[ "$1" == "--plugin-dir" ]] && plugin="$2"; shift; done
turns=20
if [[ -n "$plugin" ]]; then
  turns=12
  grep -q "## Verify" "$plugin/skills/render/SKILL.md" && turns=15
  grep -q -- "--sample per-type" "$plugin/skills/render/SKILL.md" && turns=17
fi
printf '%%PDF-1.4 fake\n' > report.pdf
cat <<JSON
{"num_turns": $turns, "total_cost_usd": 0.$turns, "duration_ms": 30000,
 "usage": {"input_tokens": 5, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 50000,
           "cache_read_input_tokens": $((turns * 40000)), "output_tokens": 4000}}
JSON

PATH="$PWD/bench/fake:$PATH" bench/bench.sh 2
# ...
# rupa          turns -40%   cost -40%
# rupa-pertype  turns -15%   cost -15%
# rupa-verify   turns -25%   cost -25%

Those numbers come from the stand-in, not from Claude.

Then run the pilot, one run per arm, and check the transcripts:

chmod +x bench/bench.sh
bench/bench.sh

Prompts live in bench/tasks/, one file per task, and TASK=<name> picks one (default report, the two-page prose report). guide is a harder three-page task with a five-column table, a CLI example and a 25-line JSON policy, closer to where hand-written HTML has to work for its layout. tight is the guide squeezed into two pages: the required parts alone fit only at tight type, so any real prose goes over the budget and the run has to cut. It exists to test how Rupa runs cut, so run it on the Rupa arms only: ARMS="rupa rupa-verify" picks which arms run (default all four). Each results folder is named after its task and keeps a copy of the prompt in task.txt.

If all four arms behaved, run three per arm on a pinned model:

MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 bench/bench.sh 3

Record the medians in your README with the date, model and task. If a Rupa arm isn't cheaper, read its transcript before changing anything else.

Step 10: What to build next

In rough order of value:

  1. Re-run TASK=guide to confirm the height-based cut estimate brings the cut rounds down to one. Then a harder benchmark task (tables, code, a wide table that must be split), where hand-written HTML should struggle more than it did on a two-page prose report.
  2. A second theme, such as your dark slate and cyan look for screen HTML, with its own reference pages and a test that renders and verifies every theme.
  3. A golden-render test in CI that verifies the sample document against its own references, so a CSS change that breaks the look fails the build.
  4. Callouts (note, warning) through a small markdown-it plugin, so Claude never needs raw HTML for them.
  5. A --watch mode for live preview while you edit by hand.
  6. More targets (DOCX through python-docx) behind the same contract and exit codes.
  7. Harness integration. Rupa is a plain CLI, so the Pramā harness can call it the same way Claude Code does.

Turning the build into a showcase

If this becomes a second project about how you built Rupa, capture material as you go rather than reconstructing it afterward.

  • One commit per milestone, with the milestone number in the message. The git log becomes the outline.
  • A decision log. The Key decisions table in Part 1 is the start; add a row whenever you change your mind, with the reason.
  • The numbers. The three-arm tables, with model, date and task. Lead with turns: that's the finding.
  • Before and after artifacts. The same report produced by hand-written HTML and by Rupa, side by side.
  • The failures. The WeasyPrint BaseException trap, the API change, the background rectangle, and the code wrap that only the visual review caught are exactly the kind of detail that makes a build write-up credible.
  • The verification records. Each verify.json and its sheets show what was checked and what was found. The appendix of this document is one.

A natural shape for a write-up or Loom entry: the problem (each turn re-reads everything, and markup work adds turns), the split (content versus form), the contract, the verification loop, the measurement, and what the numbers showed. The showcase can itself be rendered by Rupa.

Appendix: Verification record

This is the record of verifying this document with the loop it describes. Each pass ran rupa verify with the default wants, then a visual review of the sheets against the rubric. The verdicts are Claude's, written one line per sheet as the skill asks.

Pass 1: the first delivered version

The first version ran to 31 pages, before the verification sections existed.

Code checks: verify: 7/8 checks pass (FAIL near-empty p11,30); 5 sheets

Sheet Verdict
p1 cover PASS
p7 table PASS
p11 prose FAIL page balance: one table row (Sustainability) alone on a page before Part 3
p21 code FAIL overflow: CSS lines broken mid-word, 1px s / olid
p30 prose FAIL page balance: the last four items of a list alone on a page before the closing part

Two of the three failures were also flagged by the code checks. The third, the mid-word break, was visible only in the image: the text stayed inside the margins, so overflow passed.

Fixes. The lone row was a content fix: Cost optimization and Sustainability became one row. The list tail resolved once the new sections moved the page breaks. The mid-word break could only be fixed in the theme, so the loop would have reported it rather than patched it. It was fixed by hand in print.css (plain pre-wrap), and the long lines in the source files were shortened.

Pass 2: after adding verification

Code checks: verify: 8/8 checks pass; 4 sheets

All four rendered pages passed. The review failed the reference instead: the code reference showed the top of a code block that continued onto a sixth page, so the comparison was against half a page. An edit to the sample document had added blank lines. The sample was trimmed, and rupa refs now refuses a sample whose page for any type spills over. Two tests cover that.

Final pass

Code checks: verify: 8/8 checks pass; 4 sheets for visual review in verify/

Sheet Verdict
p1 cover PASS
p10 table PASS
p12 prose PASS
p39 code PASS

Cost of this pass: 4 sheets at about 2,000 input tokens each, against roughly 176,000 tokens to look at all 64 pages at full resolution.
